gary_2026_09_19_trust_in_the_hiring_funn.title: Trust In The Hiring Funnel Hackathon
gary_2026_09_19_trust_in_the_hiring_funn.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_09_19_trust_in_the_hiring_funn.summary: Gary's Guide: Event Description Generative AI broke hiring on both sides at once. Recruiters can't tell which applicants are real, & candidates can't tell which employers are. Come spend a day building something that fixes it - with the founders, engineers, & TA practitioners who live this problem every week. This is a full-day, in-person hackathon co-hosted by localhost:nyc, Integral Recruiting (IRD), & NYU - where builders team up with real talent-acquisition operators to ship working tools against a single, focused challenge. The Challenge: Trust in the Hiring Funnel Hiring has a trust crisis on both sides of the funnel - recruiters can't tell which applicants are real, & candidates can't tell which employers are. Talent acquisition runs on a basic assumption: that the person applying is who they say they are, & that the company reaching out is who it says it is. Generative AI has broken both halves of that assumption at once. Your job for the day is to rebuild it. You can attack either side of the funnel - or the seam between them. Side A - Trust coming in: the applicant flood. A role that used to draw 30 applicants now draws 500, & a growing share aren't real, aren't qualified, or are gaming the system. Candidates embed hidden prompt-injection text to manipulate the AI tools that screen resumes. And increasingly, applicants appear qualified but look strikingly alike - the same phrasing, the same structure, the same accomplishments - a tell that everyone is leaning on the same AI tools to write their applications. Recruiters are drowning, & the tools meant to help have no clear winner yet. The challenge: reliably separate real, qualified humans from AI-inflated noise - without punishing legitimate candidates who simply used AI to polish their resume. Questions worth chasing: What signals - behavioral, identity, provenance - actually distinguish a real applicant from a manufactured one? When applications converge on the same AI-generated look, how do you tell genuine signal from sameness? How do you detect a manipulated or machine-generated application without false-flagging honest people? How do you surface the candidates who deserve attention fast, inside an existing recruiting workflow rather than replacing it? Side B - Trust going out: impersonation & candidate scams. Bad actors register look-alike domains to send fake offer letters, run deepfake recruiter calls, & scam job seekers out of money & data. Employers have almost no way to detect it or warn candidates. The challenge: make it harder to impersonate a real employer, & easier for a candidate to verify that an offer or a recruiter is genuine. Questions worth chasing: How would a candidate confirm that an offer or outreach is legitimately from the company? Can impersonating domains be detected & flagged early? What does a lightweight "trust signal" look like on a careers page or an offer letter? What a strong build looks like. A working tool that raises trust in the funnel & fits the way hiring actually happens - a triage or screening layer that plugs into an existing applicant tracking system rather than replacing it, or a candidate/employer verification tool that makes impersonation harder to pull off & easier to catch. We care more about a real, demonstrable solution to a narrow slice of the problem than a broad concept that doesn't run. You don't need HR or recruiting-software experience to compete here - that's the point of a single, focused theme. Engineers & builders can go straight at the detection, identity, & verification problems. HR-technology practitioners will be in the room to keep your build grounded in how hiring actually works, & to pressure-test whether a recruiter would trust what you've made. What to Expect A full day of building - 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM, hard stop Small teams (or solo if you insist) working in one shared room TA practitioners from the SAI community in the room to keep your build grounded in how hiring really works A panel of expert judges: HR-tech founders, operators, & system admins who know these problems cold End-of-day demos to judges, investors, & real TA leaders The strongest teams get connected to investors - and, over time, to real customers Prizes Winners walk away with build-tool & platform credits, expert consulting sessions, & investor time. Everyone in the room gets connections that outlast the day - this is a room full of builders & buyers. Judges Tiffany Jin: Eqo. Building in the employee-referral & hiring space; brings a founder's eye for what actually ships. Steven Grover: Partnerspring. Operator & builder in the HR-tech ecosystem. Shane Papp: Ex-iCIMS. Deep insider knowledge of the ATS world these tools have to live inside. Adam Treitler: Related Industries. HR-tech operator with a practitioner's view of the funnel. Shiv Jethi - Engineer at SpaceX. Olivia Iarmak - Meta Reality Labs. AI quality & operations leader; researcher. Brings a practitioner's lens to trustworthy AI. D. J. Patel - VC | 3x exited founder. Prince Rumi - Excelsior Edge Ventures, Partner | AI Researcher Rami Abouemira, formerly People Ops at Square & VMware, now building the future of work with All Good HR & Founders Foundry. Ishaan Das (TechBrig) - Leads AI transformation & product design for several recruiting firms & recruiting SaaS like SquarePeg. More judges to be announced - investors & TA buyers joining the panel. Who Should Attend Engineers - full-stack, backend, frontend, AI/ML Founders & aspiring founders who like shipping fast Recent grads, master's students, & NYC college builders TA ops & recruiting-systems practitioners who want to build alongside engineers HR / recruiting professionals newer to the space - join a team as a product advisor You do not need HR or recruiting-software experience to compete - that's the whole point of one focused theme. Engineers go straight at the detection, identity, & verification problems; practitioners keep it real. Just show up ready to build. Credit Sponsors Solari is the world's fastest agent infrastructure provider. Run headless browsers, sandboxes, & desktops from one API, & automate at scale. Block Convey is an AI reliability & observability platform for AI agents. It helps teams see what an agent is doing across model calls, tools, retrieval & decisions, identify where it fails, & improve it. Hosts Somya Gupta: The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Integral Recruiting (IRD): Enterprise talent-acquisition & iCIMS/ATS specialists, & stewards of the ~350-member SAI community of TA operators & system admins. Greg Mendez: NYU. Bringing the university's builder & HR-analytics community into the room. TechSHRM is NYU Tandon's, award-winning student chapter of the Society for Human Resource Management (SHRM). Established in 1987, we bridge data science, technology, & organizational strategy through people analytics - leveraging data to optimize workforce decision-making, recruitment, & employee performance.

gary_2026_09_21_building_for_the_future_.title: Building For The Future - Data Centers, Water Stewardship & Decarbonization
gary_2026_09_21_building_for_the_future_.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_09_21_building_for_the_future_.summary: Gary's Guide: Two of the hardest problems in corporate climate action right now are water & energy, & both are being tested in real time by companies making infrastructure decisions with long lifespans. This event brings together cross-sector practitioners to discuss what's working, what's stuck, & what needs to change to achieve meaningful, shared solutions at scale. Panel one - data centers & water: Water is an increasing source of tension as data center development accelerates. Data center developers are setting water positive commitments that include reducing water demand & increasing reuse, & also investing in water replenishment that goes beyond the fenceline to invest in watersheds. In this panel, we will bring together speakers representing hyperscalers, utilities, & communities to explore what is needed to effectively support communities & ecosystems while reducing data center risks. Panel two - portfolio decarbonization: Setting a corporate emissions target is straightforward; delivering it across a portfolio of facilities built over decades is not. Public & private sector panelists will discuss how large organizations sequence capital across sites with different ages, uses, & local grids - where electrification pencils out, where it doesn't yet, & what actually moves a portfolio rather than a single flagship building.

gary_2026_09_21_when_data_goes_dark_prep.title: When Data Goes Dark - Preparing For Climate Disasters In Era Of Science Disinvestment
gary_2026_09_21_when_data_goes_dark_prep.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_09_21_when_data_goes_dark_prep.summary: Gary's Guide: Over the past year, climate science & environmental data & tools have faced steep disinvestment, but maintaining a strong scientific enterprise & the data it creates is critical to helping communities & businesses prepare for & respond to climate risks. When that data disappears, so does our ability to anticipate, prepare for, & respond to climate disasters before they strike. This panel starts by looking at what's been lost, & at the rescue efforts now underway to preserve high-fidelity climate data & disaster-cost datasets before they disappear for good. It then turns forward: what will it take to rebuild a more resilient, connected environmental data ecosystem - one built so that this kind of loss can't happen again? Join us for a conversation that moves from triage to reimagining, bringing together leaders in climate science, environmental data, global research, & emergency management to chart what comes next. Sponsored By: American Geophysical Union Climate Central The New York Climate Exchange Open Environmental Data Project

gary_2026_09_22_powering_the_ai_build_ou.summary: Gary's Guide: CleanMax invites you to a moderated panel bringing together hyperscalers, independent power producers & other market participants to examine how India's rapidly scaling data-centre sector will meet its power demand-and what role renewable energy, storage & firm-power structures need to play in getting there. What the panel will explore The scale & geography of India's data-centre power demand-and what a realistic, bankable renewable-energy pipeline could look like through 2030. Whether renewables & storage can deliver 24/7, high-reliability power at a viable cost, & where grid, transmission, land & infrastructure constraints could limit new capacity. How hyperscalers & power producers are structuring supply-from physical & group-captive arrangements to VPPAs & CFDs-and which models are becoming genuinely bankable. The broader policy & regulatory clarity needed to accelerate investment & give developers, buyers & financiers confidence in long-term delivery. How data-centre growth can earn community acceptance & support sustainable development through transparent engagement & meaningful local benefits around land, water, infrastructure & livelihoods. gary_2026_09_22_how_data_center_fights_r.title: How Data Center Fights Renewing Local Power Across US
gary_2026_09_22_how_data_center_fights_r.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_09_22_how_data_center_fights_r.summary: Gary's Guide: This is an in-person event happening as part of NYC Climate Week. To hear many in the tech industry tell it, data centers will bring wealth & prosperity not only to those who build them, but to the communities that ultimately live with & around them. However, drawing a longer historical arc is essential: AI is proposed as a new industrial moonshot in communities that have already seen the rise & fall of steel factories, coal plants, fracking infrastructure, & more. jc_culture_10004836_2026_10_04_rent_the_.title: RENT: The Musical
jc_culture_10004836_2026_10_04_rent_the_.label: Music / Movies
jc_culture_10004836_2026_10_04_rent_the_.place: ART HOUSE, 345 MARIN BLVD, JERSEY CITY
jc_culture_10004836_2026_10_04_rent_the_.summary: Experience the groundbreaking Tony Award-winning musical and Pulitzer Prize-winning drama that defined a generation. Presented at Art House Productions during the 30th anniversary year of its original premiere, RENT follows a vibrant community of artists, musicians, and dreamers in New York City’s East Village as they pursue their passions, navigate love and loss, and strive to make a meaningful impact on the world around them. Set against the backdrop of the AIDS crisis, poverty, addiction, economic uncertainty, and a rapidly changing city, these artists discover the power of friendship, the importance of creative expression, and the enduring strength of community. Featuring iconic songs and an unforgettable rock score, RENT celebrates resilience, human connection, and the transformative role of the arts in times of hardship. This production is especially meaningful as part of Art House Productions’ 25th Anniversary Season. Founded in the wake of September 11, 2001, Art House was created to bring people together through the arts during a time of profound loss and uncertainty. Thirty years after its premiere, RENT remains as relevant, timeless, and inspiring as ever, reminding us all to measure our lives in love.

jc_culture_10003571_2026_10_07_hamilton_.title: Hamilton Park Farmers Market 2026
jc_culture_10003571_2026_10_07_hamilton_.label: Festival / Market
jc_culture_10003571_2026_10_07_hamilton_.place: Hamilton Park, 9 McWilliams Pl., Jersey City, NJ
jc_culture_10003571_2026_10_07_hamilton_.summary: Join us at the Hamilton Park Farmers Market, your midweek destination for fresh, local, and thoughtfully crafted food and goods. Each week, we’re proud to feature farm-fresh produce from Stony Hill Farm alongside a curated selection of specialty vendors. Browse a variety of offerings including our long time vendor Pickles and Olives, fresh seafood from Scale Fish Market, and prepared foods perfect for dinner. You can also find baked goods, candles, personal care products, and more. You can even take advantage of convenient services like on-site knife sharpening while you shop. On the first and second Wednesdays of each month, enjoy live entertainment that adds to the vibrant, community atmosphere of the market. Whether you’re shopping for the week, grabbing a bite, or simply enjoying the park, the Hamilton Park Farmers Market is a welcoming space to connect with local vendors and neighbors.
